rationales: The first three periods are called short periods, not the fourth and fifth.
The fourth and fifth periods are classified as long periods.
The fourth and fifth periods are long, not very long.
The sixth period is called very long, not the fourth or fifth.
N₂ has a triple covalent bond between its nitrogen atoms.
O₂ has a double covalent bond, not a triple bond.
H₂ has a single covalent bond.
Cl₂ has a single covalent bond.
NH₃ has a complete octet around its nitrogen atom.
N₂ has a complete octet around each nitrogen atom.
BF₃ is electron deficient because boron has only six electrons in its valence shell.
O₂ has a complete octet around each oxygen atom.
Hydrogen has the lowest molar mass among these gases, so it diffuses fastest.
Helium is lighter than fluorine and chlorine but heavier than hydrogen.
Fluorine has a greater molar mass than hydrogen and helium, so it diffuses more slowly.
Chlorine has the greatest molar mass here, so it diffuses slowest.
Toothpaste is generally classified as a colloid, not a suspension.
Milk is an emulsion, a type of colloid.
Chalk does not dissolve in water and forms a suspension.
Blood is a complex mixture, not the standard example of a suspension intended here.
Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, represented as Fe₂O₃·nH₂O.
Fe₂O₃ alone does not represent the water of hydration in rust.
Fe(OH)₃ is not the usual formula given for rust.
Rust is represented as hydrated iron oxide, not hydrated iron hydroxide.
Alkali metals have the general outer configuration ns¹.
Alkaline earth metals have the general outer configuration ns².
The boron family generally has the outer configuration ns²np¹.
The carbon family generally has the outer configuration ns²np².
Ion making is not the result described by the attraction between atoms becoming dominant.
Bond breakage involves separation of bonded atoms, not their coming together.
Dominant attractive forces between atoms can bring them together to form a bond.
Polarity describes unequal charge distribution and is not the result asked for.
A triple covalent bond contains six shared electrons, not eight.
Three shared pairs make a total of six electrons.
Four electrons make two shared pairs, which form a double bond.
Five electrons cannot form three complete shared pairs.
Milk of Magnesia is not a true solution because magnesium hydroxide does not dissolve fully.
It is not classified as a colloid in this context.
It is not a saturated solution; undissolved magnesium hydroxide is dispersed in water.
Milk of Magnesia is a suspension of magnesium hydroxide in water.
For equal volumes of solution, 2 M is the most concentrated and contains the least water relative to solute.
A 1 M solution is less concentrated than a 2 M solution.
A 0.5 M solution is less concentrated than 1 M and 2 M solutions.
A 0.25 M solution is the most dilute and contains the most water relative to solute.
Carbon is oxidized, so the reaction is not oxidation alone.
Zinc oxide is reduced, but carbon is oxidized in the same reaction.
Both oxidation and reduction occur, so the reaction is redox.
No electrolysis is involved because the reaction is not driven by an electric current.
Sulphuric acid solution conducts electricity by forming ions.
Sugar solution does not form ions in water and is a non-electrolyte.
Calcium hydroxide solution contains ions and acts as an electrolyte.
Sodium chloride solution contains mobile ions and is an electrolyte.
Potassium is highly reactive and is more reactive than silver.
Aluminium is more reactive than silver.
Lead is more reactive than silver.
Silver is the least reactive metal among these options.
H₂O₃ is not the formula of hydrogen peroxide.
Hydrogen peroxide has the formula H₂O₂.
H₂O is the formula of water.
HO is not the formula of hydrogen peroxide.
